title: Repackage GPU kernel bundles and implement deterministic fallback paths for mixed-driver fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our runtime currently bundles multiple kernel variants (CUTLASS/Triton-backed) in an ad-hoc layout which causes slow probe paths, sporadic ABI mismatch errors on fleets with mixed driver versions, and poor cold-start latency for new model families. Several customer incidents in the last 6 months (Dedicated and Private) traced back to nondeterministic kernel selection and missing signed binaries.

Goal: Repackage kernel artifacts into a deterministic on-disk layout + versioned manifest, add a signed-bundle option for Private/VPC installs, and implement a deterministic fallback selection algorithm that minimizes probe cost and guarantees a safe runtime path for mixed-driver fleets. Deliver measurable latency and error reductions and CI gating to prevent regressions.

Scope:
- Rework artifact layout: flat manifest-driven bundles with metadata (abi-tag, driver-min, cutlass-variant, digest).
- Implement runtime loader that reads manifest and selects primary candidate via compatibility ranking, with at most two probe attempts before falling back to a safe, slower generic kernel compiled with minimal dependencies.
- Add optional bundle signing and verification for Private installs (integrates with KMS-managed keys).
- CI: add compatibility matrix tests that run small kernels across driver permutations (NVidia driver container matrix) and enforce no silent fallback regressions.
- Backwards compatibility: support old layout for two release cycles via a compatibility adapter.

Acceptance criteria:
- Probe latency (first-token path) reduced by >=50% on mixed-driver test harness compared to baseline (baseline: median probe 42ms).
- Cold-start kernel load reduced from ~210ms to <=80ms for common model families.
- No increase in kernel fallback-related errors in canary (slo: <0.1% of requests with kernel-selection errors).
- Signed bundles validated end-to-end on Private staging with KMS key.
- CI matrix catches at least one previously unseen incompatibility before merge (tests included in PRs).

Implementation notes / tradeoffs:
- Deterministic strategy chooses the highest-capability kernel whose driver_min <= host_driver and abi_tag matches. We avoid trying every variant to keep probes cheap. That means some exotic combinations might require the fallback generic kernel; acceptable given safety tradeoff.
- Signed bundles add operational overhead for self-hosted customers (key rotation), so we make signing opt-in per-deployment.
- We will keep an adapter layer to support the legacy layout for two releases to avoid destabilizing long-lived Private clusters.

Key files & artifacts:
- Design spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/GPU/Kernel+Bundle+Manifest+Spec
- Draft API for manifest and loader: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4721
- Compatibility test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/compat-test-suite/tree/eng-102345

Rollout plan:
1) Merge runtime loader and manifest reader behind feature flag (runtime-1.23-canary).
2) Build signed bundles for staging nodes and validate KMS flows (Private staging).
3) Canary on 5% of hosted traffic (no signing) for two weeks, monitor kernel-selection errors and latency.
4) Roll to Dedicated pools with opt-in toggles for customers and run compatibility job per-customer fleet.
5) Deprecate legacy adapter after 2 releases with migration docs.

Monitoring & KPIs:
- metric/kernel_probe_latency_ms (histogram)
- metric/kernel_selection_errors_total
- trace/kernel_selection.path (for sampling problematic hosts)
- Canary dashboard: compare pre/post percentiles and error rates.

Notes on testing: we will run the compatibility matrix on an internal matrix of drivers: 510.47, 525.x, 535.x, and containerized driver stubs for older pinned hosts used by Private customers. Each matrix cell executes a small training/inference kernel and validates output bit-exactness where expected, otherwise validates graceful fallback and no crash.
